research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Explores Deskovic falsely confessing after lengthy interrogation as a teen; Exonerated by DNA after 16 years; Established foundation. Available via ABC.
research_notes_other.research_findings: While a specific 20/20 episode titled "Confession at Gunpoint" wasn't confirmed, the details of Jeffrey Deskovic's case match the description perfectly. His case is a prominent example of a coerced false confession from a juvenile, despite exculpatory DNA evidence being available even before trial.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Rape and Murder (of 15-year-old classmate Angela Correa in 1989)
featured_individuals.sentence: 15 years to life (Information from external knowledge, common case detail)
contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confession (interrogated at 16 for 6+ hours, polygraphs, no parent/lawyer), police pressure, ignoring exculpatory DNA evidence pre-trial
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated by DNA evidence (which identified the actual perpetrator, Steven Cunningham); Declared Actually Innocent
organizations_involved_raw: Innocence Project; Founded the Jeffrey Deskovic Foundation for Justice
